title: API contract first
brief: Before an agent implements an endpoint, pin down the contract. Given a feature, output ONLY a JSON object: {"method": HTTP verb, "path": REST path, "request_body": object of field → type (or null), "responses": {status code: description}}. Responses must include the correct success code and at least one 4xx error.

lesson.summary: Agreeing the contract first (method, path, request shape, status codes) gives the implementing agent a precise target and gives you something to test against. It also surfaces design questions, like what 404 means here, before code exists.
lesson.why_it_matters: Schema-first design is how backend teams parallelize work: frontend, backend, and test agents can all build against the same contract. Correct status codes are part of the contract, not an afterthought.
lesson.strong_example:
Design the REST endpoint for: {{feature}}
Return ONLY JSON: {"method", "path", "request_body": {field: type} or null, "responses": {"<code>": description}}. Use the correct success code (201 for creation, 204 for deletion) and include 4xx errors.

vars.feature: Create a new todo item with a title and an optional due date.

checks.label: Output is valid JSON with nothing else around it

test_cases.golden_output: {"method": "POST", "path": "/todos", "request_body": {"title": "string", "due_date": "string (YYYY-MM-DD), optional"}, "responses": {"201": "Todo created; returns the new todo", "400": "Missing or empty title", "422": "Invalid due_date format"}}

vars.feature: Fetch a single order by its id.

checks.label: Output is valid JSON with nothing else around it

test_cases.golden_output: {"method": "GET", "path": "/orders/{order_id}", "request_body": null, "responses": {"200": "The order", "404": "No order with that id"}}

vars.feature: Delete a comment that the current user wrote.

checks.label: Output is valid JSON with nothing else around it
Handles comments the user can't delete

test_cases.golden_output: {"method": "DELETE", "path": "/comments/{comment_id}", "request_body": null, "responses": {"204": "Comment deleted", "403": "The comment belongs to another user", "404": "No comment with that id"}}

rubric: The contract follows REST conventions and covers the realistic failure cases
hints: If a frontend developer built against your output today, what would they still have to guess?
This is schema-first design. Fix the exact JSON shape, and state the conventions you expect: verbs per action, resource-style paths, and correct status codes including errors.
Try: 'Return ONLY JSON {method, path, request_body, responses}. POST creates (201), GET reads (200, 404 if missing), DELETE removes (204). Always include the relevant 4xx errors.'
reference_prompt:
You are an API designer. Design one REST endpoint for this feature: {{feature}}

Return ONLY a JSON object (no markdown, no explanation) with exactly these keys:
- "method": the HTTP verb (POST to create, GET to read, PATCH/PUT to update, DELETE to remove)
- "path": a plural resource path, using {id}-style placeholders
- "request_body": an object mapping field names to types, or null if there is no body
- "responses": an object mapping status codes (as strings) to short descriptions

Use the correct success code (201 Created for creation, 200 for reads, 204 for deletes) and include every realistic 4xx error: 400/422 for invalid input, 403 for forbidden, 404 for not found.
